correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed the sharp bound. If the origin changes on the second application, the sites of S changed on the first form a nonempty subset T of S1. Their initial active copies agree on overlaps and with the target pattern off T. For any compatible T, its compatible nonempty subsets are precisely its nonempty outgoing-edge-closed subsets in the graph t→s with s−t a nonzero zero-offset. With at most one such offset an extreme point is a sink, so witness size >1 costs at least three zero-sites. For S0={−2,0,2} and the odd interval progression starting at 5, translated copies agree by parity and miss S0; the adjacent ±2 edges make the whole fiber strongly connected. The indicator of T+T supplies the explicit two-step witness. For m=2,3,4, the rightmost-one interval pattern has a compatible singleton and the indicator of {2(m−1)} witnesses non-idempotence. Every noncentral coordinate is essential by toggling it in the active pattern, and the origin is essential when any noncentral coordinate mismatches. This verifies the claim for actual minimal memory.
residual_risks: The proof is for finite binary unique-active-transition rules on Z; no interval-width, higher-alphabet, or algorithmic lower bound follows. Recorded finite checks are supplementary.
